- scripts/review_findings_record.py:324-334 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, z-ai_glm-5_3-flash]
  PROBLEM: In parse_review_issues, the `passthrough_blocks_skipped` check (`if PASSTHROUGH_START_RE.match(line)`) runs inside the parse loop. That loop exits at `if len(issues) >= MAX_ISSUES: truncated = True; break` when it reaches the 501st issue header. review_parse_consolidator.sh line 969 (`cat "${parsed_blocks_file}" "${passthrough_file}" > "${REVIEW_ISSUES_FILE}"`) always appends passthrough blocks after the parsed blocks, so once the cap trips the loop never reaches them.
  WHY: A round with more than 500 parsed issues plus uncovered reviewer anchors gets a record that has `issues_truncated` but no `passthrough_blocks_skipped`, which contradicts the agents fragment (`agents.d/chatgpt-review-findings-record.md`) and the log-prefix registry. All four reviewers rated it SEVERITY: NIT, mapped here to low; there was no disagreement. The suggested fix is about 2 lines: run one regex search over `text` before or after the loop, or check in the truncation branch.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/review_findings_record.py:parse_review_issues | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The passthrough warning check sits at the top of the `for line in text.splitlines():` loop, and the cap branch `if len(issues) >= MAX_ISSUES: truncated = True; break` exits that loop. scripts/review_parse_consolidator.sh line 969 runs `cat "${parsed_blocks_file}" "${passthrough_file}" > "${REVIEW_ISSUES_FILE}"`, and lines 954-962 write the passthrough blocks as `=== ISSUE PASSTHROUGH ${pass_code} ===`. Passthrough blocks therefore always come after the parsed blocks.
  WHY: With more than 500 issues plus uncovered anchors, the record carries `issues_truncated` but not `passthrough_blocks_skipped`, which contradicts the agents fragment. Suggested fix: a whole-text `re.search(r"(?m)^=== ISSUE PASSTHROUGH [0-9]+ ===$", text)`, or read `passthrough_blocks=<n>` from the parser stats file (write_stats line 34). Impact is low because it only happens above the cap. The reviewer also gave this as a hardening suggestion (2 lines, HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1).
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

- scripts/review_findings_record.py:parse_review_issues for-loop | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The passthrough-block warning is only checked inside the issue-parsing loop, and that loop breaks after 500 issues. `review_parse_consolidator.sh` concatenates `passthrough_file` AFTER `parsed_blocks_file` (line 969, `cat "${parsed_blocks_file}" "${passthrough_file}" > "${REVIEW_ISSUES_FILE}"`), so once the cap is reached the warning is never added.
  WHY: With more than 500 issues plus any uncovered reviewer anchor, `warnings` omits `passthrough_blocks_skipped`, which contradicts `agents.d/chatgpt-review-findings-record.md` and the log-prefix registry. Operators cannot tell from `warnings` that passthrough blocks were skipped. The reviewer also gave this as a hardening suggestion: run one whole-text regex scan before the loop, or replace the `break` with a flag and a final scan (2 lines, HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1).

  WHY: With more than 500 parsed issues plus uncovered reviewer anchors, the record reports `issues_truncated` but omits `passthrough_blocks_skipped`, so it understates what was left out. Suggested fix (1-2 lines): move detection out of the loop, or add the check in the truncation branch.
